Source_Title: Panel 'Kepulangan ke Tanahair' (the voyage home, 1977)
Author_or_Organisation: Royal Malaysian Navy (TLDM) display on board KD Hang Tuah
Document_Reference: Photograph IMG_8987.HEIC (iPhone 16), taken on board KD Hang Tuah, 30 September 2026, centre panel
Rights_Status: Panel content belongs to its producer. Photograph unpublished pending the project owner's review.
Verification_Notes: Panel text documents: departure from Portsmouth 15 Aug 1977 at 3.00 pm; calls at Jeddah (10–17 Sep, Umrah and Hari Raya Aidilfitri), Abu Dhabi, Muscat and Colombo; arrival at Port Klang 14 Oct 1977 at 9.00 am; Malacca 16–17 Oct; Woodlands 18 Oct 1977. The panel map additionally labels Casablanca, Tunisia and Alexandria (no dates) and gives planned ETA/ETD times. The map label 'Abu Dabi, Saudi Arabia' is geographically wrong (Abu Dhabi is in the UAE). Producer and date of the panel are not shown. Claims on this panel are marked Verified only where the panel text states them directly.

Source_Title: Panel 'Pengenjinan Semula KD HANG TUAH' (re-engining)
Author_or_Organisation: Royal Malaysian Navy (TLDM) display on board KD Hang Tuah
Document_Reference: Photograph IMG_8987.HEIC (iPhone 16), taken on board KD Hang Tuah, 30 September 2026, left panel
Rights_Status: Panel content belongs to its producer. Photograph unpublished pending the project owner's review.
Verification_Notes: Documents: Docking Essential Defect (DED) repairs at Naval Dockyard Sdn Bhd (year cut off in photo); original eight ASR1 16 VTS main engines and four ASR1 8 LTS generators; ministerial approval August 1994; contract to Wärtsilä 22 August 1995 (two 12SW28 main engines, three generator sets, model only partly legible); tow to MSE Pasir Gudang 9 October 1995; cost RM24 million; accepted February 1997. The right edge of the panel is cut off in the photograph — re-photograph to read the missing words.

Source_Title: KD Hang Tuah to be turned into naval museum
Author_or_Organisation: Bernama (republished by The Borneo Post, 22 November 2018)
Verification_Notes: Commissioned 22 July 1977; asset of the 21st Frigate Squadron; oldest ship in the fleet; about 500,000 km sailed; declared a naval museum on 21 November 2018 by the Chief of Navy; opening then expected early 2019. Describes the ship as 'over 50 years old' (counting from her 1966 launch).

Source_Title: Museum Ship of the Navy
Verification_Notes: States the ship was designated the navy's museum ship on 21 November and that she was NOT being decommissioned: she kept her commission. Publication year not printed on the page.

Source_Title: KD Hang Tuah tamat perkhidmatan selepas hampir lima dekad
Verification_Notes: Decommissioning ceremony at Lumut naval base, 3 December 2025, officiated by Western Fleet Commander Vice Admiral Datuk Baharudin Wan Md Nor. Commissioned 22 July 1977. Reports the ship focused mainly on training 'from the 1980s' and lists exercises Malindo Jaya, Emas Hitam, Milan, Kakadu and LIMA (undated). Gives beam as 12.02 m (other sources: 12.2 m).

Source_Title: KD Hang Tuah decommissioned after five decades of service
Verification_Notes: Confirms date, place and officiating officer; ship's bell tolled and ensign lowered.

Source_Title: Malaysia Phases Out Cold War Frigate KD Hang Tuah
Verification_Notes: Confirms decommissioning on 3 December 2025 as part of the '15 to 5' programme. Rest of article paywalled.

Source_Title: Memorial Muzium Kapal Diraja Hang Tuah tarikan baharu pelancongan di Lumut
Verification_Notes: Handover to the Perak state government on 27 July 2026 at Himpitan 1, Lumut naval base; PPP between MB Inc. and Aero Art Sdn Bhd; Phase 1 about RM30 million; opening expected 2027. Also states service ended 3 December 2025.

Source_Title: KD Hang Tuah Memorial Museum to become Lumut's new tourist attraction
Verification_Notes: Confirms the handover and 2027 opening. Sole source for the claim that the ship took part in Ops Fajar in the Gulf of Aden in 2009 (unconfirmed).

Source_Title: Frigate to open as Perak ship museum in 2027

Source_Title: MERMAID — vessel record
Document_Reference: Read from the screenshot 'documen hng tuah.png' (the site blocks automated access)
Verification_Notes: Launched 29/12/1966; completed 16/05/1973; Yarrow & Co. Ltd., Scotstoun, yard no 2284; 2,300 displacement; length 344 ft 9 in LOA (conflicts with 103.5 m elsewhere); breadth 40 ft; draft 12 ft (conflicts with 4.9 m); 8 Admiralty Standard Range 16-cyl diesels, 14,400 bhp, 24 knots; transferred to Malaysia May 1977 (others: April); commissioned as KD Hang Tuah August 1977 after a refit at Vosper Thornycroft (others: 22 July 1977).

Source_Title: HMS Mermaid
Verification_Notes: Ordered by Ghana as Black Star; about £5 million; launched without ceremony 29 Dec 1966; Type 41/61 basis, flush deck, single funnel; Mk XIX twin 4 in, four 40 mm, Squid mortar; sonars 170 and 176; 2,300 tons; 24 knots; complement 177; to Portsmouth April 1972, Chatham refit; commissioned 16 May 1973; based in Singapore; stood by for Saigon evacuation; Fittleton collision; Cod Wars; MTI radar trials; transferred April 1977 keeping F76.

Source_Title: F 76 HMS Mermaid
Verification_Notes: Launched 29 Dec 1966; commissioned 16 May 1973; transferred April 1977; training ship 1992; 1995–97 refit. Internally inconsistent on displacement (2,300 vs 2,340 t) and crew (177 vs 210).

Source_Title: HMS Mermaid (1966)
Verification_Notes: USE WITH CAUTION — contains clear errors: says she was 'decommissioned on May 1973'; dates the Saigon evacuation to 1973 and says she carried it out; calls the ASW weapon both Squid and Limbo; says the museum can be visited today. Used only as the sole source for laid down 1965, range 4,800 nm/18 kn and 9,928 bhp after refit, all marked Needs Verification.

Source_Title: Last of the Yarrow diesel tin cans gets a reprieve (Warship Wednesday)
Verification_Notes: Ordered 1964; completed 1967; about £3.8 million of Crown loans written off 1971; collision with ICGV Thor, March 1976 (caption); 4-inch gun replaced by 57 mm Bofors in 1992. Blog — used for alternative dates only.

Source_Title: HMS Fittleton memorial (M4165)

Source_Title: Worst Royal Naval Reserve collision remembered
Verification_Notes: Fittleton was trying to come alongside Mermaid; capsized in under a minute; 12 died, 11 of them RNR volunteers; en route to Hamburg.
